purpose: The pid-to-liveness contract, written once and executed as a table. Every combination of (roster complete?, pid in use?, start time recorded?, start time matches?, pid looks like an agent?) has a row here, so a case cannot be handled by accident or forgotten in a refactor. tests/process-liveness.test.ts runs these through src/server/process-liveness.ts and separately asserts the table is exhaustive.
invariants: `gone` is only ever reached from evidence about THIS process: the number is unused, or a recorded start time disagrees with the observed one. Never from failing to recognise a command.
An unrecorded start time can only produce `alive` or `unverifiable`, never `gone`. Weak evidence may keep a session on the board; it may never bury one.
An incomplete roster answers `unverifiable` for everything, whatever else is known.

cases.name: an incomplete roster cannot speak, even about a pid it saw
cases.claim: A probe that did not finish is a gap, not an observation. This outranks every other row.

cases.name: an incomplete roster does not bury a pid that is missing from it
cases.claim: The dangerous half of the row above: absence in a partial scan must not read as death.

cases.name: a number nothing holds is gone
cases.claim: The strongest ending evidence there is, and the only one that depends on recognising nothing.

cases.name: a number nothing holds is gone even with no start time recorded
cases.claim: Provenance is needed to tell processes apart, not to notice that none exists.

cases.name: a matching start time is alive
cases.claim: The one path that actually proves the number still refers to what we attributed.

cases.name: a mismatched start time is gone, however agent-like the holder
cases.claim: Our process exited and the kernel handed the number on. A fact about this session, so it may say gone.

cases.name: a mismatched start time is gone when a daemon holds the number
cases.claim: Measured: pid 90614, recorded by a claude session, later `sysextd`. This is the row that retires it honestly.

cases.name: no start time plus an agent holding the number is presumed alive
cases.claim: Coverage was 55/86 claude and 21/55 codex records, so refusing this path would mass-retire a live fleet. Weak, and deliberately only ever positive.

cases.name: no start time and a non-agent holding the number is unknown, not dead
cases.claim: Measured: pid 59458, recorded by a claude session, later `/usr/libexec/siriknowledged`, live on the board for 33 hours. Unknown, because nothing witnessed the ending and the number is genuinely in use.

cases.name: no start time and no way to tell what holds the number is unknown
cases.claim: A roster that lists presence but not commands cannot support the presumption either way.

cases.name: a recorded start time the roster cannot corroborate falls back to the agent presumption
cases.claim: Presence-only rosters (identity.ts has no start times) must still work, and must not read a missing corroboration as disagreement.

cases.name: a recorded start time the roster cannot corroborate, held by a non-agent, is unknown
cases.claim: The recycled-pid case as it reaches the stale-pid fallbacks, which have presence but no start times.

cases.name: a roster that knows nothing at all cannot answer
cases.claim: Neither presence nor starts. Complete in the sense that the scan finished, but it enumerated nothing usable.
